opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin on Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted. Max for full-time employee without owning role is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training (HR note says full-time; conflicting). Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin, so recommend read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requested admin access to Source Code. Admin is never permitted for this request: Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Robert is a Payroll Specialist, so even under the HR note (full-time) the maximum is write. The Security note conflicts, listing Robert as a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read (admin never allowed for contractors). Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum under either interpretation, I grant the more restrictive permitted maximum, read, which is safe under both notes.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Robert Weber (E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (from HR?): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation for Source Code: write. Comment says Source Code is owned by Engineer role, so admin not permitted. Max for full-time employee without owning role is write. Recommend write.
- Note 2 (from Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read. Comment says Security DB shows contractor with basic training, max read; admin never allowed. Requested admin, so recommend read.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor.

The notes indicate conflicting facts. How should the approver decide? The policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system. Source Code owned by Engineer, Robert is Payroll Specialist, so max write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Robert has basic training, so max read.

The requested level is admin. Based on either note, admin is not permitted. Maximum is either write (if full-time/Payroll Specialist) or read (if contractor with basic training). Never grant more than requested; requested admin is above max, so grant max.

Which max? Given conflicting facts, the safer/more restrictive decision is read (from security). The Security agent's note says contractor with basic training, max read. The HR note says full-time, max write. Given conflict, granting the lower level (read) is the conservative choice that satisfies both interpretations (read ≤ write).

So decision: read.

Evidence: conflicting employment info; both notes agree admin is not allowed. Security note says contractor with basic training → max read. So grant read, which is within both the full-time max (write) and contractor max (read). Actually read is at or below both maximums, so grant requested level? Wait, requested is admin, but max is read per security note, so grant max = read.

Let me submit read.
